pacts/blade.name: Pact of the Blade
pacts/blade.description:
Use a Bonus Action to conjure a Simple or Martial melee weapon in your hand or bond with a magic weapon you touch. Do not bond a weapon attuned to someone else or bonded to another Warlock. While bonded, you are proficient with it and can use it as a Warlock spellcasting focus. For its attacks and damage, you may use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity. You may choose its normal damage type, Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant on an attack.

You may also bind an existing ordinary nonmagical melee weapon; it becomes magical as a Pact weapon. For this test, apply the same Bonus Action and bond-ending rules as the modern Blade baseline. The bond ends when you use this bonding Bonus Action again, the weapon remains more than 5 feet away for one minute, or you die. A conjured weapon then disappears. A physical weapon remains present.
pacts/blade.deepenedAtLevel5: At Warlock 5, your Attack action can make two Pact-weapon attacks. This is intrinsic and costs no Invocation. Devouring Blade can later raise this to three total attacks. Thirsting Blade can not be selected; its extra attack is already part of this Pact. Extra Attack features do not automatically add their attack counts together. Weapon Mastery, disarm immunity, and no-throw restrictions are not automatic Blade benefits.

pacts/chain.name: Pact of the Chain
pacts/chain.description:
Learn Find Familiar without spending an ordinary spell selection. This test uses its 5.5e Chain mode: cast it as a Magic action without a slot, while retaining the spell's required components. Its ritual route remains available. Choose a special form: Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Skeleton, Sphinx of Wonder, Sprite, or Venomous Snake. The normal animal forms from Find Familiar are also available. Use the relevant host-game references and tell us which statblock version you used.

The familiar shares your initiative but tracks its own turn, movement, action, and Reaction. Order the two turns together. Without an attack command, it can perform permitted non-Attack tasks normally. When you take the Attack action, forgo one of your attacks to command one familiar Attack action on its turn in that shared initiative round. At Warlock 5, that action contains two attacks. It does not gain a second Attack action or use its Reaction for this class command route.

Investment of the Chain Master can alternatively command that same action with your Bonus Action. Using both routes does not create another familiar Attack action. There is at most one commanded familiar Attack action per shared initiative round. The Warlock's ordinary Action stays available when the Bonus Action route is used. For this test, give the command before the familiar's attack resolution. Special non-Attack actions follow their statblocks; no blanket spell or summon action grant is created.
pacts/chain.deepenedAtLevel5: At Warlock 5, the familiar makes two attacks in its one commanded Attack action. It does not gain a second Attack action. The base Attack-action command and Investment of the Chain Master Bonus Action command share the same single commanded Attack action per shared initiative round.

pacts/tome.name: Pact of the Tome
pacts/tome.description:
Conjure your Book of Shadows at the end of a Short or Long Rest. Only you access its Pact magic. It disappears when replaced or you die. While carrying it, gain three additional cantrips from any class spell list and two level-1 Ritual spells you do not otherwise know. They count as Warlock spells and the book is a focus. When a replacement book appears, choose its starter spells again; this does not replace ordinary known spells or recharge its limited uses.

This test resolves the ritual boundary conservatively: starter Ritual spells are available as rituals, not as extra normal Pact-slot spells unless independently known. A ritual adds ten minutes to normal casting time and spends no slot; it still requires components and concentration where applicable. This procedural restriction is proposed, because the 5.5e version can support broader slot casting. Book of Ancient Secrets separately buys discovered higher ritual inscription; it does not give a second starter pair.
pacts/tome.deepenedAtLevel5: At Warlock 5, gain one separate slot-free level-3 casting each of Animate Dead, Haste, and Call Lightning per Long Rest. Retain components, casting times, durations, concentration, and creature commands. These are three independent uses, not a shared pool. This test does not add them to normal Pact-slot casting unless separately learned. Replacing the book never recharges these uses.

pacts/talisman.name: Pact of the Talisman
pacts/talisman.description:
Receive one active magical talisman and wear it or give it to another creature.

Untrained Guidance: the wearer can add 1d4 to an ability check using a skill in which they are not proficient, with no charge limit.

Fortunate Correction: after failing any ability check, the wearer may spend one charge to add 1d4 and potentially succeed. A single check can benefit from only one of these two effects, never both. They do not modify attacks or saving throws.

Core charges equal your Warlock proficiency bonus and return on Long Rest.

Replace a lost talisman with a one-hour ceremony during a Short or Long Rest. The old one becomes inactive. Replacement or transfer does not restore charges. Rebuke, Protection, and Bond are elective, never intrinsic; those three options are not included in this version of the test.
pacts/talisman.deepenedAtLevel5: Shared Ward uses your Reaction and one of the same core charges when the wearer within 60 feet takes damage. Reduce that one instance by 2d6 + your Charisma modifier, minimum zero reduction and no more than incoming damage. You may be the wearer; sight of the attacker is not required.

patrons/fiend.name: The Fiend
patrons/fiend.description: Fiend supplies signature abilities and spell access. Any of the four active Pacts can belong to this Patron. The host Fiend's level-10 selected-type resistance and Hellfire Shield are not granted. Universal Energy Resistance remains.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.description: When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 HP, or another creature reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 HP, gain temporary HP equal to max(1, Charisma modifier + Warlock level). Use normal host temporary HP rules; these do not stack or restore ordinary HP.

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.description: After an ability check or saving throw is rolled, before its outcome resolves, add 1d10, at most once per roll. Uses equal max(1, Charisma modifier), recovered on Long Rest. It costs no Reaction and does not modify attacks.

features.name: Infernal Retaliation
features.description:
Spend your Reaction at a time you choose and the single shared use per Long Rest. Choose one mode for 20 rounds (two minutes). Continuing it needs no more Reactions. No external trigger is required to activate it; an unconscious Warlock can not do so.

Fiendish Resilience. Heal 1 HP/round at Warlock 8, 2 at 13, or 5 at 18. Reaching 0 HP while it is already active stabilizes you once without restoring HP or consciousness. It does not heal at 0 HP, revive the dead, or stabilize again after further damage. If another effect restores you above 0, remaining healing can resume.

Fiendish Flamewreath. After each resolved melee hit against you from a creature within 5 feet, that creature takes the listed Fire damage. Separate multiattack hits can each qualify. No save or additional Reaction is required. Misses, ranged hits, and ongoing damage do not trigger it.

At Warlock levels 8, 13, and 18, healing is respectively 1, 2, and 5 HP per round; Fire damage is respectively 1d6, 2d6, and 5d6 per qualifying hit.

Provisional timing: healing ticks at your turn start above 0 HP, first on your next turn. Count twenty turn-starts, including those spent at 0 without healing. Flamewreath ends at the twentieth subsequent turn start.

features.name: Infernal Retaliation Improvement
features.description: Increase Resilience healing to 2 HP per round or Flamewreath Fire damage to 2d6 per qualifying hit; no additional use.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.description:
Once per turn on a qualifying attack-roll hit, expend its use and force a Charisma save against your spell DC. On failure the target travels through the Lower Planes and is Incapacitated; if not a Fiend, it immediately takes 8d10 Psychic damage. While absent it is unavailable to ordinary targeting. It returns at the end of your next turn to its departed space or the nearest unoccupied space. Success still spends the use.

Recover on Long Rest or spend a Pact slot to restore a use. For this test restoration costs no additional action and stores at most one use; that action timing is provisional.

features.name: Infernal Retaliation Improvement
features.description: Increase Resilience to 5 HP per round or Flamewreath to 5d6 Fire per qualifying hit; no additional use.

spellAccess.description:
Automatically know the Fiend spells at their listed Warlock levels without ordinary selection costs or daily preparation. They grant no extra slots or free casts. If a normal spell choice later becomes automatic, restore that choice for another eligible spell.

No Patron spells are automatically learned at Warlock 1; the first five arrive at 3.

invocations/devouring-blade.name: Devouring Blade
invocations/devouring-blade.description: Your Blade Pact and its intrinsic level-5 two-attack feature are required. When you take the Attack action with your Pact weapon, make three attacks total instead of two. This is one upgrade, not three extra attacks.

definition.description: A Patron supplies Warlock power, a Pact is the type or manifestation of its agreement, and Invocations are additional terms attached to that Pact. This selected modular design is under active testing alongside coherent native classes; it is not a source edition candidate or a finalized architecture decision.

improvements: Energy Resistance increases to 10 for each of your two chosen damage types.

limitations: The host 5e/5.5e rules supply spell details, equipment, feats, creatures and ordinary combat mechanics for this standalone alpha.
Companion control, crafting checks, and some shared effects remain subject to host-game adjudication.
Star Chain / Seeker remains disabled; Talisman's three elective Invocations and four other omissions are not available in Alpha 0.3.1.
Infernal Retaliation tick timing and Hurl Through Hell slot recharge action cost are provisional.
Alternative Invocation progressions are reference comparisons, not simultaneous grants.
No Band 2 or automatic Epic Boon at level 19.
referenceNotes: Use the host 5e or 5.5e origin, ability-score, starting equipment, feat, and leveling rules with these class traits. A Magic action uses your Action when playing in 5e.
Invocation totals exclude the free Pact. Cantrip totals exclude automatic Eldritch Blast and Pact grants. Spells known exclude automatic Patron, Pact, and Mystic Arcanum grants.
Related Fiend milestones below describe the current playtest Patron. They are not additional base-class grants and do not award those features twice.

definition.description:
Know two Warlock cantrips and two level-1 Warlock spells. Choose from your host Warlock list plus explicit class grants. Your spell attack modifier is proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier; spell save DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier.

All Pact slots have the level shown in the class table. Spend one to cast an eligible known Warlock spell of that level or lower, applying its higher-slot rules. Regain all Pact slots on a Short or Long Rest. Use host casting/rest rules. These spells are known without daily preparation.

When the table increases ordinary cantrips or spells known, choose the difference; newly chosen leveled spells can not exceed your Pact slot level. On gaining a Warlock level, you may replace one ordinary cantrip and one ordinary known spell with eligible alternatives. Patron, Pact, and Arcanum grants are separate.

You automatically gain Eldritch Blast in addition to your ordinary cantrip choices. Use your host game's version of the cantrip. It counts as a Warlock cantrip for Invocation prerequisites. Do not spend another cantrip choice to learn it, and do not add historical 3.5e blast dice to its beams.

For a single-class Warlock, its beam count is one at level 1, two at level 5, three at level 11, and four at level 17. Resolve each beam's attack, damage, and possible critical separately under the host rules.

Your magic has a continuing Patron source, which may be inherited, involuntary, or unknown by name. Direct communication or a literal contract is unnecessary. Choose Fiend for this round and gain its features at their listed levels. Do not add another Patron package at level 3.

Your Pact establishes the type or manifestation of your deal with your Patron. Choose one Pact: Blade, Chain, Tome, or Talisman. This choice costs no Invocation selection. Each Pact gains an intrinsic improvement at Warlock 5. The Pact section explains its abilities. Additional simultaneous Pacts are outside this round.

Learn one eligible Invocation, an additional term attached to your larger Pact. Gain additional selections when the class table increases your total. Each costs one elective selection, attaches to your actual Pact, and requires that Pact's Patron to accept it. Existing or inherited terms may supply acceptance without a new conversation.

Meet every level, Pact, cantrip, and other prerequisite. A generic option can attach to any eligible Pact; it is not unattached. Repeat an option only if permitted by its text. On gaining a Warlock level, you may replace one Invocation with an eligible alternative, keeping prerequisites required by retained choices.

A severed Pact suspends its Invocations, preserving acquisition history without an automatic refund. Restoration or transfer requires valid receiving terms, Patron acceptance, and prerequisite revalidation.

Perform an esoteric rite for one minute. Restore expended Pact Magic slots up to half your maximum, rounded up: one at levels 2-10 or two at levels 11-20. Once used, you must finish a Long Rest to use the rite again. It does not refill other resources. Eldritch Master improves this same rite at level 20.

Reduce Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from weapons or natural attacks by 1 per damage instance, including magical weapons unless they are cold iron. Cold iron bypasses this reduction. It does not reduce a separately typed Fire, Force, or other damage rider.

The reduction increases to 2 at Warlock 7, 3 at 11, 4 at 15, and 5 at 19. For this test, apply flat mitigation before ordinary half-damage Resistance, rounding down after halving. Do not apply the same flat benefit twice to one damage component.

Increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1, to a maximum of 20, or choose an eligible feat using your table's normal rules. Gain this feature again at Warlock 8, 12, 16, and 19. Use an ordinary eligible improvement at 19 for this round; Epic Boons remain outside this test.

On eligible magic-item-use competency checks, you may treat the d20 as 10 even while threatened or distracted, then add normal modifiers. This does not grant automatic success or apply to attacks, saves, or unrelated skills.

For this test, use Charisma + proficiency if proficient in your table's applicable magic-item-use competency; otherwise use Charisma. If the host lacks that check procedure, leave this ability untested rather than introducing another skill system.

Gain your Pact's intrinsic improvement without spending an Invocation: Blade makes two Pact-weapon attacks with its Attack action; Chain's commanded familiar Attack action contains two attacks; Tome gains its three separate slot-free spell uses; Talisman gains Shared Ward. Read the full rule in your Pact entry.

Know Contact Other Plane in addition to your ordinary selections. Once per Long Rest, cast it without a slot to contact your Patron, automatically succeeding on its saving throw. Normal casting time and other spell restrictions remain. Direct communication is not the first acquisition of your Patron's identity.

Permanently choose two damage types from Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, and Thunder. Reduce damage of each chosen type by 5 per instance. This increases to 10 at Warlock 20.

This is flat mitigation, not ordinary 5e/5.5e half-damage Resistance. Apply it before any ordinary Resistance and round down after halving. It is a universal class feature, separate from the Fiend's omitted level-10 selected-type resistance.

Choose one level-6 Warlock spell. Cast it once without a spell slot, recovering its use on a Long Rest. Each Arcanum has its own one-use-per-Long-Rest allowance at its own spell level. They are not Pact slots and do not upcast one another or consume ordinary known-spell selections.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you may replace one Arcanum spell with another Warlock spell of the same level.

With the required item-creation entitlement, substitute a magic-item-use check for a missing prerequisite spell: DC 15 + spell level for arcane, or DC 25 + spell level for divine. Other requirements and costs remain.

Failure does not complete the item or consume its creation payment. Do not retry that substitution until your next Warlock level. If the host lacks the crafting/check procedure, leave this feature untested.

Choose one level-7 Warlock spell. Cast it once without a spell slot, recovering its use on a Long Rest. Each Arcanum has its own one-use-per-Long-Rest allowance at its own spell level. They are not Pact slots and do not upcast one another or consume ordinary known-spell selections.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you may replace one Arcanum spell with another Warlock spell of the same level.

Choose one level-8 Warlock spell. Cast it once without a spell slot, recovering its use on a Long Rest. Each Arcanum has its own one-use-per-Long-Rest allowance at its own spell level. They are not Pact slots and do not upcast one another or consume ordinary known-spell selections.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you may replace one Arcanum spell with another Warlock spell of the same level.

Choose one level-9 Warlock spell. Cast it once without a spell slot, recovering its use on a Long Rest. Each Arcanum has its own one-use-per-Long-Rest allowance at its own spell level. They are not Pact slots and do not upcast one another or consume ordinary known-spell selections.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you may replace one Arcanum spell with another Warlock spell of the same level.
Magical Cunning now restores all your expended Pact Magic slots. It remains the same once-per-Long-Rest, one-minute rite, not a second recovery resource.

invocations/investment-of-the-chain-mast.name: Investment of the Chain Master
invocations/investment-of-the-chain-mast.description: Your Bonus Action can command the familiar's one allowed Attack action instead of sacrificing an attack. Do not use both pathways for extra familiar actions. Choose a 40-foot Fly or Swim speed, preserving superior base speed. When it deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you may replace that damage with Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant. Its forced saves use your Warlock spell DC. When it takes damage, spend your Reaction to give it Resistance against that one damage instance. This does not add an Attack action or refill limited attacks.

invocations/gift-of-the-protectors.name: Gift of the Protectors
invocations/gift-of-the-protectors.description: Your Book of Shadows can hold up to max(1, Charisma modifier) willing creatures' names. When a named creature would drop to 0 HP without dying outright, it drops to 1 HP instead. This rescue uses one shared page use per Long Rest, not one per name. A creature writes its own name over one minute; erase a name with a Magic action. No Talisman or Tome free-spell resource is spent.

invocations/book-of-ancient-secrets.name: Book of Ancient Secrets
invocations/book-of-ancient-secrets.description: Discover and transcribe additional Ritual spells of level no greater than half your Warlock level rounded up. Pay 50 gp and spend two hours per spell level. You can cast them as rituals through the active book; this does not add ordinary known spells or free nonritual casts. No additional starting pair is granted. Paid ritual records survive book replacement without adding new spells or restoring uses.

invocations/agonizing-blast.name: Agonizing Blast
invocations/agonizing-blast.description:
Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls.

Repeatable: You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

Track the chosen cantrip by name. Each further purchase must enhance a different eligible cantrip. Automatic Eldritch Blast qualifies.
invocations/agonizing-blast.cantripPrerequisite: A known Warlock cantrip that deals damage.
